prompt:
A 0.50 kg block is pressed against a spring of spring constant 300 N/m on a horizontal, frictionless surface, compressing the spring by 0.20 m. The block is released. After leaving the spring, it slides across a rough section of the surface 1.0 m long (coefficient of kinetic friction 0.30), and then up a frictionless ramp. Use $g=9.8$ m/s^2.

**(a)** Calculate the speed of the block as it leaves the spring.

**(b)** Calculate the amount of mechanical energy converted to thermal energy as the block crosses the rough section.

**(c)** Calculate the speed of the block when it leaves the rough section.

**(d)** Calculate the maximum height above the horizontal surface that the block reaches on the ramp.

rubric.description: (a) Equates the spring energy $\frac12kx^2=6.0$ J to the kinetic energy $\frac12mv^2$
(c) Finds the remaining kinetic energy $6.0-1.47=4.53$ J and the speed $\approx4.3$ m/s
(d) Equates the remaining kinetic energy to $mgh$ and finds $h\approx0.92$ m

sampleResponse:
(a) $\frac12kx^2=\frac12mv^2$: $\frac12(300)(0.20)^2=6.0$ J $=\frac12(0.50)v^2$, so $v=\sqrt{24}\approx4.9$ m/s.
(b) The friction force is $\mu mg=(0.30)(0.50)(9.8)=1.47$ N over 1.0 m, so 1.47 J becomes thermal energy.
(c) $KE=6.0-1.47=4.53$ J, so $\frac12(0.50)v^2=4.53$ and $v=\sqrt{18.1}\approx4.3$ m/s.
(d) At the top of the ramp all of the remaining kinetic energy is potential energy: $mgh=4.53$ J, so $h=\frac{4.53}{(0.50)(9.8)}\approx0.92$ m.

prompt:
A 1000 kg car on a level road accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 25 m/s in 6.0 s. Ignore friction and air resistance.

**(a)** Calculate the change in the car's kinetic energy.

**(b)** Calculate the average power delivered to the car by the engine during this time.

**(c)** Calculate the distance traveled by the car during the 6.0 s, and use it to find the average net force on the car.

**(d)** Calculate the instantaneous power the engine delivers at the end of the 6.0 s, and explain why it is greater than the average power.

rubric.description: (c) Finds the average force $\frac{\Delta KE}{d}=2500$ N
(d) Computes $P=Fv=(2500)(25)=6.25\times10^4$ W and explains that the speed (and so the power for a constant force) is increasing

sampleResponse:
(a) $\Delta KE=\frac12(1000)(25^2-10^2)=\frac12(1000)(525)=2.6\times10^5$ J.
(b) $P_{avg}=\frac{\Delta KE}{t}=\frac{262\,500}{6.0}\approx4.4\times10^4$ W (44 kW).
(c) With uniform acceleration the average speed is $\frac{10+25}{2}=17.5$ m/s, so the distance is $(17.5)(6.0)=105$ m. $F_{net}=\frac{\Delta KE}{d}=\frac{262\,500}{105}=2500$ N (which equals $ma=1000\times2.5$).
(d) With a constant force of 2500 N, $P=Fv=(2500)(25)=6.25\times10^4$ W. The power $Fv$ increases as the car speeds up, so at the end it is larger than the average over the interval, which includes the slower speeds near the start.
